## TIP-OFF

is our opening huddle where coaches welcome the players as a group and set the expectations for the day. The Tip-Off should take no longer than 5 minutes to maximize player's attention spans. There are 5 parts that should be covered in every Tip-Off:

### CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

### CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

### COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

### COMMENCEMENT

Players are primed and prepped for the start of the camp.

### CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together! "NBA Basketball School on 3! (Location Name) on 6!"

PARTNER TAG GAME

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no basket needed)

#### EQUIPMENT

None needed. Can add 1 ball per player for dribbling loads.

#### DESCRIPTION

Give players 10 seconds to find a partner. On "go," both players attempt to tag their partner's knees simultaneously. Play tag for 30 to 60 seconds. Each player should keep track of how many tags they get. Change partners after two loads have been applied to tag games.

#### SCORING

Players get 1 point for tag.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Scanning and reading the playing area
- Creativity
- Changing speed and direction
- Deking and juking

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- While moving, tag partner's back.
- While crawling, tag partner's back.
- While hopping on one leg, tag partner's hips.
- While jumping on two legs, tag partner's hips.
- While dribbling, tag partner's knees.
- While dribbling, only use weak hand to tag partner's hips.
- While dribbling, steal their partner's ball.
- While dribbling, each player must keep one foot on part of any line within the gym while still trying to steal their partner's ball. Both feet off the line leads to a point for the partner.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Encourage players to find a way to tag your opponent, while avoiding being tagged.
- Ensure players change partners after every two rounds.
- Watch for kids who have their head down and encourage them to keep eyes up.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

?

- "What are the best ways to fake someone out?"
- "Why is changing speeds important?"

4-ON-2 PASSING RONDO

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no basket needed). Mark out squares using 4 cones with every cone approximately 6 steps away.

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball and 4 cones per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Four players will act as passers, who cannot move and must stand over the cones. Two defenders stand in the middle. The passers have to keep the ball away from the defenders. A defender switches with a passer if they tag the player with the ball, deflect a pass, or steal a ball. This game can also be played 4-on-3, 5-on-2, 5-on-3, etc. subject to group numbers and space. Each load can be played for 2 to 3 minutes.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Say the name of the teammate you pass to.
- Can only take one dribble.
- Can only pass with one hand.
- After making a pass, exchange spots with a teammate.
- Continually move around in the space (e.g. 4-on-2 keepaway).

#### SCORING

Not needed due to warm-up. Players get 1 point for every completed pass (if desired).

#### STAFF ROLE

- Mark out squares with cones quickly and efficiently so players do not waste time waiting.
- Ensure players switch roles so players experience both offense and defense.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Identifying the open player
- Faking a pass then making a pass
- Changing angle of pass

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Where was the open player?"
- "What can you do to be surprising on defense?"

### I-ON-I BLIND

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Players find a partner and a ball. Two groups can play 1-on-1 on the same basket at the same time. The defender will start 'blind' to the offense, with their heels on the 3PT line facing the basket. The offense will hold the ball and place it on the defender's back. Once they lift the ball from the defense's back, it becomes a live 1-on-1. The offense has a maximum of three dribbles to score. Only one shot is allowed. The players are responsible for rotating and resetting the activity: the next group can begin once the defense is in the 'blind' position and they see clear space. Each repetition should have a different starting location around the 3PT line.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound, blocked shot, or forced turnover).

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating and maintaining advantage
- Exploring different types of finishes
- Attacking the basket at different angles

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Add dribbles.
- The defense cannot jump.
- The offense and defense must change partners after they both play offense.
- The offense can only score at the rim inside the paint.
- The offense can only score using the net.
- The offense can only score using the backboard.
- The offense can only score using their weak hand.
- The offense can only score off two feet.
- Defense starts side by side with the offensive player (smaller advantage).

#### STAFF ROLE

- Get the players organized to read the space and successfully organize themselves by communicating whose turn it is (each repetition should start within two seconds of the one before finishing).
- Remind players to get back in line without disrupting the next group by going around the side.
- Challenge players to think about why they are using particular finishes.
- Make sure players drive from different angles and locations.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you improve your initial move to create and keep the advantage?"
- "How can you prevent the defender from recovering?"
- "Are there any adjustments that need to be made with your finish?"

### 2-ON-2 CHANGING LOCATIONS

16 MIN
BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets.

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Players find a partner. Each basket needs one ball and several groups. One group will begin on offense anywhere outside the 3PT line with a second group of defenders matching up. Other groups will wait their turn at the baseline. The on-ball defender will start 'blind' to the offense, with their heels on the 3PT line facing the basket. The offense will hold the ball and place it on the defender's back. The off-ball defender can start in a gap or help position depending on their match up's placement on the 3PT line. As soon as the offense lifts the ball from the defense's back, it becomes a live 2-on-2. Games go until a basket is scored, there is a defensive stop, or the ball goes out of bounds.

#### SCORING

Offensive teams will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Keeping and maintaining advantage
- Attacking the help defense
- Scoring off 2-on-1 advantages
- Stunting and recovering
- Stopping the ball

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "What other positions could you explore playing from?"
- "What can the defense do to ensure the offense does not score off the first drive?"

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- The offense can only score a rim finish or 3PT shot.
- For younger players, the mid-range is still permitted.
- Escape the lava. After a pass or cut is completed, the offensive player without the ball has three seconds to escape the lava (space out). If they are still inside the lava after three seconds, a turnover is called.
- After a made basket, the next team waiting at the baseline must inbound it against the team that just scored. The defenders must pressure the ball (this may include aggressively attempting to double team the receiver). The offense has five seconds to complete a successful inbounds pass. Play stops if the offense is able to inbound the ball. If the defense intercepts the ball, they can score it immediately to gain additional points.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Help players explore varied spacings, ensuring they begin from different positions.
- Officiate the 'lava' load.

I-ON-I+I GRAB AND PLAY

IG MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

2 balls per group

### DESCRIPTION

Players work in groups of five. An offensive player will begin in a corner with a defensive player standing in front of them. The player will pass to the initiator who is positioned a single gap away on the wing. As the ball is received, the initiator will put the ball on their inside hip, while placing their outside hand out for the defender to hi-five. The offensive player will sprint to grab the ball while the defender sprints to hi-five the initiator and recover in front of the offensive player in a live 1-on-1. As soon as the first 1-on-1 is played, the next two players start their 1-on-1 in the same format. The initiator should facilitate four games of 1-on-1 before the pairings change in each group and a new initiator is chosen.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points for made baskets.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Keeping the advantage before the defense recovers to neutral
- Defense recovering from a disadvantage

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Give the defense a hi-five further away to increase the offensive advantage.
- Players have two dribbles to score.
- The facilitator can pivot cueing the offensive player to curl. The defender must chase over - they are not allowed to go under.
- The offensive player is allowed to cut backdoor as opposed to grabbing the ball. In this case, the facilitator must pass the ball. On a cut, the defender does not need to continue sprinting to the defender to hi-five, but must immediately recover.

### STAFF ROLE

- Help players facilitate correctly, placing the ball on the inside hip and their outside hand ready for the hi-five.
- Groups on each basket may stagger to avoid collisions.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Can you push the ball out further to gain enhanced separation?"
- "When is a good time to cut backdoor?"

VARIABLE SHOOTING

IG MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

### DESCRIPTION

Players work in pairs. They must shoot 6 shots, with the shooter and rebounder staying in the same role. Once 6 shots are taken, both players will change roles. To begin with, players focus on shooting every shot from a different range and location, while passing in a variable manner in different ways and from changing locations and distances.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Use a smaller ball and shoot from a closer distance with younger players.
- Players must shoot with different arcs (low arc, normal arc, high arc).
- Players must shoot from different stances (wide, narrow, one leg, staggered, etc.).
- Players must shoot while performing a different dribble move before each shot.
- Players must shoot out of different movements (e.g. lunges, hops, crawls, hand-stands, etc.).

### SCORING

N/A

### STAFF ROLE

- Encourage players to explore different shooting coordinations
- Remind players to continuously change where they shoot and pass from

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Adaptive shooting

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you make each movement more variable?"

4-ON-4 CHANGING RIMS GAME

20 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available full-courts

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per court

### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of four players based on the number of courts available. Try to have a maximum of five teams on each full-court. In instances of very high numbers, half-courts can be used. Teams play to three baskets. After a team scores three baskets, they get 1 point. The losing team will rotate off while the next team waiting rotates on. The team that gets a point gets to maintain possession and stay on offense: they will need to immediately attack the opposite end of the court. The game is then continually played, with teams keeping track of their total number of points over the course of the activity.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The changing rims load: when the offense crosses the half-court line, they can change the basket in which they are attacking at any time. The entire team must cross the half-court line to change direction.

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure quick changes after one team secures the win and a new team sprints on-court. They do not need to wait for the defense to get ready, but can immediately inbound the ball and commence play.
- Explain the changing rims load.

### SCORING

3 baskets = 1 point for team.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating space and keeping advantage
- Ball movement
- Emergency transition defense

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- When is a good time to pass in a 2-on-1?
- How can you space the floor effectively?

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of five players based on the number of courts available. Try to have a maximum of five teams on each full-court. In instances of very high numbers, half-courts can be used. Teams play to three baskets. After a team scores three baskets, they get a point. The losing team rotates off while the next team waiting rotates on. The game is then continually played, with teams keeping track of their total number of points over the course of the activity.

### SCORING

3 baskets = 1 point for team.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Maintaining excellent spacing
- Looking to contain defensive match-ups 1-on-1

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How can you get the most efficient shot?
- How can we help teammates to emphasize continuous ball pressure?
- What can you do to space the floor effectively?

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- Pass and cut is a turnover. Players can only create an advantage through a static 1-on-1 where the ball-handler creates an advantage with a dribble move from the perimeter, or through a post-up. Teammates should maintain spacing (following the lava load), ready to receive the ball.
- Double teams that lead to turnovers result in an extra 3 points.
- No ball pressure results in the defensive team losing 1 point and the offense regaining possession on the sideline.

### STAFF ROLE

- Organize the waiting teams on the sideline so teams transition quickly for the next repetition.
- Ensure players substitute every few minutes.
- Emphasize and teach offensive and defensive concepts and philosophy.

- Encourage players to be creative exploring different movements as part of their warm-up.

- "How many different ways can you move?"
- "How can you disguise your change of speed?"

3-ON-3, SCORE THROUGH A 1-ON-1

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

### DESCRIPTION

Three offensive players will space in varied locations outside the 3PT line with three defenders guarding them and a team of three waiting along the baseline. The offense has a 14 second shot clock to score. If the defense gains possession (defensive rebound or forced turnover), they must clear the ball before the shot clock starts again. On a score, the team that gets scored on rotates off, while the new team sprints onto defense. Players can only score through a 1-on-1 from the perimeter or a 1-on-1 post-up. Any other score (e.g. pass and cut, pick and roll, off-ball screen, dribble hand-off, etc.) does not count.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Driving and kicking the ball if second help defender is activated
- Creating space and keeping advantage

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- One defender must play with their hands behind their back. This is who the offense should look to target. Change the constrained defender every minute.
- After each score, the offensive players must dribble to the half-court and come back before playing the next defense.
- Different players must initiate the 1-on-1. It is a turnover if the same offensive player tries the 1-on-1 on back-to-back possessions.

### STAFF ROLE

- Count down from 14 seconds.
- Remind players they can only score through 1-on-1 from the perimeter or post.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Where is the match-up advantage greatest?"
- "Where should the help defender position themselves to be ready for the drive?"
